13: # Pi
14:
15: Pi is a minimal, extensible agent harness that you can make your own.
16:
17: Adapt Pi to your workflows, not the other way around. Customize Pi with [extensions](packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md), [skills](packages/coding-agent/docs/skills.md), [prompt templates](packages/coding-agent/docs/prompt-templates.md), and [themes](packages/coding-agent/docs/themes.md). Bundle them as [Pi packages](packages/coding-agent/docs/packages.md) and share via npm or git.
18:
19: Pi ships with powerful defaults but skips features like sub-agents and plan mode. Ask Pi to build what you want, or install a package that does it your way.
20:
21: Use Pi [interactively](packages/coding-agent/docs/usage.md), automate it in [print or JSON mode](packages/coding-agent/docs/cli.md), control it over [RPC](packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc.md), or build apps with the [Pi TypeScript SDK](packages/coding-agent/docs/sdk.md). See [OpenClaw](https://github.com/OpenClaw/OpenClaw) for a real-world integration.
22:
23: ## Getting started
24:
25: Install the command-line interface:
26:
27: ```bash
28: curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh
29: ```
30:
31: On Windows:
32:
33: ```shell
34: powershell -c "irm https://pi.dev/install.ps1 | iex"
35: ```
36:
37: The installer pins all dependencies and updates Pi with `pi update`. Alternatively, install directly with npm, which does not pin transitive dependencies:
38:
39: ```bash
40: npm install -g --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
41: ```
42:
43: Pi requires Node.js 22.19 or newer. The macOS, Linux, and Windows installers can install it if needed. Pi does not require dependency lifecycle scripts for a normal npm installation.
44:
45: Start Pi in the directory where you want it to work:
46:
47: ```bash
48: cd /path/to/project
49: pi
50: ```
51:
52: For a built-in AI provider, run `/login` inside Pi to connect a subscription or API key. Then give Pi a task.
53:
54: See the [documentation](https://pi.dev/docs/latest) for full setup and usage instructions, or [visit pi.dev](https://pi.dev) for demos.
55:
56: ## Run with Nix
57:
58: ```bash
59: nix run github:earendil-works/pi/stable
60: ```
61:
62: `stable` points at the latest release. Install it with `nix profile add github:earendil-works/pi/stable` and update with `nix profile upgrade pi`. Use a release tag such as `github:earendil-works/pi/v1.0.0` to pin a version, or `github:earendil-works/pi` for unreleased changes on `main`. Nix builds Pi from source.
63:
64: Supports ARM64 and x86-64 on Linux and macOS. Use `nix build .` or `nix run .` to build or run your checkout.
65:
66: Nix builds are offline, so the bundled model data comes from a pi.dev model catalog revision pinned in `nix/model-catalog.json`. At runtime, Pi still overlays newer catalog data from pi.dev as usual. The Nix workflow replaces the pin on `main` when it no longer matches the checkout, for example after a provider is added or gains a new model type. To refresh it by hand:
67:
68: ```bash
69: npm run update:model-catalog-pin
70: ```

75:
76: | Package | Description |

82: | **[@earendil-works/pi-agent-core](packages/agent)** | Agent runtime with tool calling and state management |

88: ## Permissions & Containerization
89:
90: Pi does not include a built-in permission system for restricting filesystem, process, network, or credential access. By default, it runs with the permissions of the user and process that launched it.
91:
92: If you need stronger boundaries, containerize or sandbox Pi. See [packages/coding-agent/docs/containerization.md](packages/coding-agent/docs/containerization.md) for three patterns:
93:
94: - **Gondolin extension**: keep `pi` and provider auth on the host while routing built-in tools and `!` commands into a local Linux micro-VM.
95: - **Plain Docker**: run the whole `pi` process in a local container for simple isolation.
96: - **OpenShell**: run the whole `pi` process in a policy-controlled sandbox.
97:
98: ## Contributing
99:
100: See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for contribution guidelines and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for project-specific rules (for both humans and agents).  Longer term plans for Pi can also be found in [RFCs](https://rfc.earendil.com/keyword/pi).

102: ## Development
103:
104: ```bash
105: npm install --ignore-scripts  # Install all dependencies without running lifecycle scripts
106: npm run build         # Refresh model data, then build all packages
107: npm run build:offline # Rebuild using existing model data without network access
108: npm run check         # Lint, format, and type check
109: ./test.sh            # Run tests (skips LLM-dependent tests without API keys)
110: ./pi-test.sh         # Run pi from sources (can be run from any directory)
111: ```
112:
113: ### Using local packages outside the monorepo
114:
115: Build every public package into one coherent local artifact set:
116:
117: ```bash
118: npm run pack:packages -- --out .artifacts/pi-packages
119: ```
120:
121: This refreshes model data before building `pi-ai`. To avoid network access when
122: model data is already hydrated, pass `--offline-model-data`.
123:
124: Then configure an external project to consume one package and resolve all of
125: its Pi dependencies from the same artifact set. npm is the default:
126:
127: ```bash
128: node scripts/use-local-packages.mjs \
129:   --manifest .artifacts/pi-packages/manifest.json \
130:   --consumer ../my-project \
131:   --package @earendil-works/pi-durable \
132:   --package @earendil-works/pi-agent-core
133: cd ../my-project
134: npm install --ignore-scripts
135: ```
136:
137: For a pnpm project, point `--consumer` at the workspace root:
138:
139: ```bash
140: node scripts/use-local-packages.mjs \
141:   --manifest .artifacts/pi-packages/manifest.json \
142:   --consumer ../my-project \
143:   --package @earendil-works/pi-agent-core \
144:   --package-manager pnpm
145: cd ../my-project
146: pnpm install --ignore-scripts
147: ```
148:
149: Repeat `--package` for each direct dependency. The command updates the
150: consumer's `package.json` with content-addressed local `file:` references. It
151: writes transitive overrides to `package.json` for npm or `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
152: for pnpm. Keep the artifact directory available while installing or updating
153: the consumer. Re-run both commands after changing Pi source.
154:
155: ## Building standalone binaries from release source
156:
157: GitHub releases include a versioned source archive covered by the release's `SHA256SUMS` file. Extract it and run the same build script used for the official standalone binaries:
158:
159: ```bash
160: VERSION="<release-version>"
161: tar -xzf "pi-${VERSION}-source.tar.gz"
162: cd "pi-${VERSION}"
163: ./scripts/build-binaries.sh --offline-model-data --platform linux-x64 --out "$PWD/out"
164: ```
165:
166: The archive includes release model data and native prebuilds. `--offline-model-data` uses that model data without refreshing provider catalogs. The script installs dependencies and builds the executable with its runtime assets; pass `--skip-install` if dependencies are already provided.
167:
168: ## Supply-chain hardening
169:
170: We treat npm dependency changes as reviewed code changes.
171:
172: - Direct external dependencies are pinned to exact versions. Internal workspace packages remain version-ranged.
173: - `.npmrc` sets `save-exact=true` and `min-release-age=2` to avoid same-day dependency releases during npm resolution.
174: - `package-lock.json` is the dependency ground truth. Pre-commit blocks accidental lockfile commits unless `PI_ALLOW_LOCKFILE_CHANGE=1` is set.
175: - `npm run check` verifies pinned direct deps, native TypeScript import compatibility, and the generated coding-agent install lock.
176: - The pi.dev installer installs from `packages/coding-agent/install-lock/`, generated from the root lockfile, to pin transitive deps. The npm package does not pin transitive deps.
177: - Local release smoke tests and npm publication use the same tarball packer; npm publishes the validated tarballs rather than repacking workspace directories.
178: - Local release installs, documented npm installs, and `pi update --self` use `--ignore-scripts` where supported.
179: - CI installs with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, and a scheduled GitHub workflow runs `npm audit --omit=dev` plus `npm audit signatures --omit=dev`.
180: - Install lock generation has an explicit allowlist for dependency lifecycle scripts; new lifecycle-script deps fail checks until reviewed.

90: 		return "yarn";
91: 	}
92: 	if (isBunRuntime || resolvedPath.includes("/install/global/node_modules/")) {
93: 		return "bun";
94: 	}
95: 	if (resolvedPath.includes("/npm/") || resolvedPath.includes("/node_modules/")) {
96: 		return "npm";
97: 	}
98:
99: 	return "unknown";
100: }
101:
102: function getInferredNpmInstall(): { root: string; prefix: string } | undefined {
103: 	const packageDir = getPackageDir();
104: 	const path = process.platform === "win32" || packageDir.includes("\\") ? win32 : { basename, dirname };
105: 	const parent = path.dirname(packageDir);
106: 	let root: string | undefined;
107: 	if (path.basename(parent).startsWith("@") && path.basename(path.dirname(parent)) === "node_modules") {
108: 		root = path.dirname(parent);
109: 	} else if (path.basename(parent) === "node_modules") {
110: 		root = parent;
111: 	}
112: 	if (!root) return undefined;
113: 	const rootParent = path.dirname(root);
114: 	if (path.basename(rootParent) === "lib") return { root, prefix: path.dirname(rootParent) };
115: 	// Windows global npm prefixes use `<prefix>\\node_modules`, which is
116: 	// indistinguishable from local project installs by path shape alone. Do not
117: 	// infer unsupported Windows custom prefixes without `npm root -g` evidence.
118: 	return undefined;
119: }
120:
121: function getSelfUpdateCommandForMethod(
122: 	method: InstallMethod,
123: 	installedPackageName: string,
124: 	updatePackageTarget: SelfUpdatePackageTarget = installedPackageName,
125: 	npmCommand?: string[],
126: ): SelfUpdateCommand | undefined {
127: 	const target = normalizeSelfUpdatePackageTarget(updatePackageTarget);
128: 	switch (method) {
129: 		case "bun-binary":
130: 			return undefined;
131: 		case "pnpm": {
132: 			const match = readCommandOutput("pnpm", ["root", "-g"])
133: 				? undefined
134: 				: /^(.*[\\/]global[\\/][^\\/]+)[\\/]\.pnpm[\\/]/.exec(getPackageDir());
135: 			const binDirArgs = match
136: 				? [`--config.global-bin-dir=${process.env.PNPM_HOME || dirname(dirname(match[1]))}`]
137: 				: [];
138: 			return makeSelfUpdateCommand(
139: 				makeSelfUpdateCommandStep("pnpm", [
140: 					"install",
141: 					"-g",
142: 					"--ignore-scripts",
143: 					"--config.minimumReleaseAge=0",
144: 					...binDirArgs,
145: 					target.installSpec,
146: 				]),
147: 				target.packageName === installedPackageName
148: 					? undefined
149: 					: makeSelfUpdateCommandStep("pnpm", ["remove", "-g", ...binDirArgs, installedPackageName]),
150: 			);
151: 		}
152: 		case "yarn":
153: 			return makeSelfUpdateCommand(
154: 				makeSelfUpdateCommandStep("yarn", ["global", "add", "--ignore-scripts", target.installSpec]),
155: 				target.packageName === installedPackageName
156: 					? undefined
157: 					: makeSelfUpdateCommandStep("yarn", ["global", "remove", installedPackageName]),
158: 			);
159: 		case "bun":
160: 			return makeSelfUpdateCommand(
161: 				makeSelfUpdateCommandStep("bun", [
162: 					"install",
163: 					"-g",
164: 					"--ignore-scripts",
165: 					"--minimum-release-age=0",
166: 					target.installSpec,
167: 				]),
168: 				target.packageName === installedPackageName
169: 					? undefined
170: 					: makeSelfUpdateCommandStep("bun", ["uninstall", "-g", installedPackageName]),
171: 			);
172: 		case "npm": {
173: 			const [command = "npm", ...npmArgs] = npmCommand ?? [];
174: 			const inferred = npmCommand?.length ? undefined : getInferredNpmInstall();
175: 			const prefixArgs = [...npmArgs, ...(inferred ? ["--prefix", inferred.prefix] : [])];
176: 			// pi.dev advertises releases immediately, so a configured npm age gate would
177: 			// block the update. npm has no per-package age gate, so this also lets new
178: 			// transitive dependency releases through. Managed installs avoid this.
179: 			const installStep = makeSelfUpdateCommandStep(command, [
180: 				...prefixArgs,
181: 				"install",
182: 				"-g",
183: 				"--ignore-scripts",
184: 				"--min-release-age=0",
185: 				target.installSpec,
186: 			]);
187: 			const uninstallStep =
188: 				target.packageName === installedPackageName
189: 					? undefined
190: 					: makeSelfUpdateCommandStep(command, [...prefixArgs, "uninstall", "-g", installedPackageName]);
191: 			return makeSelfUpdateCommand(installStep, uninstallStep);
192: 		}
193: 		case "unknown":
194: 			return undefined;
195: 	}
196: }
197:
198: function readCommandOutput(
199: 	command: string,
200: 	args: string[],
201: 	options: { requireSuccess?: boolean } = {},
202: ): string | undefined {
203: 	const result = spawnProcessSync(command, args, {
204: 		encoding: "utf-8",
205: 		stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
206: 	});
207: 	if (result.status === 0) return result.stdout.trim() || undefined;
208: 	if (options.requireSuccess) {
209: 		const reason = result.error?.message || result.stderr.trim() || `exit code ${result.status ?? "unknown"}`;
210: 		throw new Error(`Failed to run ${[command, ...args].join(" ")}: ${reason}`);
211: 	}
212: 	return undefined;
213: }
214:
215: function getGlobalPackageRoots(method: InstallMethod, _packageName: string, npmCommand?: string[]): string[] {
216: 	switch (method) {
217: 		case "npm": {
218: 			const configured = !!npmCommand?.length;
219: 			const [command = "npm", ...npmArgs] = npmCommand ?? [];
220: 			if (configured && command === "bun") {
221: 				const bunBin = readCommandOutput(command, [...npmArgs, "pm", "bin", "-g"], {
222: 					requireSuccess: true,
223: 				});
224: 				const roots = [join(homedir(), ".bun", "install", "global", "node_modules")];
225: 				if (bunBin) {
226: 					roots.push(join(dirname(bunBin), "install", "global", "node_modules"));
227: 				}
228: 				return roots;
229: 			}
230: 			const root = readCommandOutput(command, [...npmArgs, "root", "-g"], {
231: 				requireSuccess: configured,
232: 			});
233: 			const inferred = configured ? undefined : getInferredNpmInstall();
234: 			return [root, inferred?.root].filter((x): x is string => !!x);
235: 		}
236: 		case "pnpm": {
237: 			const root = readCommandOutput("pnpm", ["root", "-g"]);
238: 			if (root) return [root, dirname(root)];
239: 			const match = /^(.*[\\/]global[\\/][^\\/]+)[\\/]\.pnpm[\\/]/.exec(getPackageDir());
240: 			return match ? [match[1]] : [];
241: 		}
242: 		case "yarn": {
243: 			const dir = readCommandOutput("yarn", ["global", "dir"]);
244: 			return dir ? [dir, join(dir, "node_modules")] : [];
245: 		}
246: 		case "bun": {
247: 			const bunBin = readCommandOutput("bun", ["pm", "bin", "-g"]);
248: 			const roots = [join(homedir(), ".bun", "install", "global", "node_modules")];
249: 			if (bunBin) {
250: 				roots.push(join(dirname(bunBin), "install", "global", "node_modules"));
251: 			}
252: 			return roots;
253: 		}
254: 		case "bun-binary":
255: 		case "unknown":
256: 			return [];
257: 	}
258: }
259:
260: function normalizeExistingPathForComparison(path: string, resolveSymlinks: boolean): string | undefined {
261: 	const resolvedPath = resolve(path);
262: 	if (!existsSync(resolvedPath)) {
263: 		return undefined;
264: 	}
265: 	let normalizedPath = resolvedPath;
266: 	if (resolveSymlinks) {
267: 		try {
268: 			normalizedPath = realpathSync(resolvedPath);
269: 		} catch {
270: 			return undefined;
271: 		}
272: 	}
273: 	if (process.platform === "win32") {
274: 		normalizedPath = normalizedPath.toLowerCase();
275: 	}
276: 	return normalizedPath;
277: }
278:
279: function getPathComparisonCandidates(path: string): string[] {
280: 	return Array.from(
281: 		new Set(
282: 			[normalizeExistingPathForComparison(path, false), normalizeExistingPathForComparison(path, true)].filter(
283: 				(candidate): candidate is string => !!candidate,
284: 			),
285: 		),
286: 	);
287: }
288:
289: function getEntrypointPackageDir(): string | undefined {
290: 	const entrypoint = process.argv[1];
291: 	if (!entrypoint) return undefined;
292: 	let dir = dirname(entrypoint);
293: 	while (dir !== dirname(dir)) {
294: 		if (existsSync(join(dir, "package.json"))) {
295: 			return dir;
296: 		}
297: 		dir = dirname(dir);
298: 	}
299: 	return undefined;
300: }
301:
302: function isSelfUpdatePathWritable(): boolean {
303: 	const packageDir = getPackageDir();
304: 	try {
305: 		accessSync(packageDir, constants.W_OK);
306: 		accessSync(dirname(packageDir), constants.W_OK);
307: 		return true;
308: 	} catch {
309: 		return false;
310: 	}
311: }
312:
313: function isManagedByGlobalPackageManager(method: InstallMethod, packageName: string, npmCommand?: string[]): boolean {
314: 	const packageDirs = [getPackageDir(), getEntrypointPackageDir()].filter((dir): dir is string => !!dir);
315: 	const packageDirCandidates = packageDirs.flatMap((dir) => getPathComparisonCandidates(dir));
316: 	return getGlobalPackageRoots(method, packageName, npmCommand).some((root) => {
317: 		return getPathComparisonCandidates(root).some((normalizedRoot) => {
318: 			const rootPrefix = normalizedRoot.endsWith(sep) ? normalizedRoot : `${normalizedRoot}${sep}`;
319: 			return packageDirCandidates.some((packageDir) => packageDir.startsWith(rootPrefix));
320: 		});
321: 	});
322: }
323:
324: export function getSelfUpdateCommand(
325: 	packageName: string,
326: 	npmCommand?: string[],
327: 	updatePackageTarget: SelfUpdatePackageTarget = packageName,
328: ): SelfUpdateCommand | undefined {
329: 	const method = detectInstallMethod();
330: 	const command = getSelfUpdateCommandForMethod(method, packageName, updatePackageTarget, npmCommand);
331: 	if (!command || !isManagedByGlobalPackageManager(method, packageName, npmCommand) || !isSelfUpdatePathWritable()) {
332: 		return undefined;
333: 	}
334: 	return command;
335: }

337: /**
338:  * The self-update command configured by the user: `PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND` (whitespace-separated
339:  * argv, no quoting), else the global `selfUpdateCommand` setting. Overrides install-method detection.
340:  */
341: export function getConfiguredSelfUpdateArgv(setting: string[] | undefined): string[] | undefined {
342: 	const fromEnv = process.env.PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND?.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
343: 	if (fromEnv?.length) return fromEnv;
344: 	return setting?.length ? setting : undefined;
345: }
346:
347: /** Fill the `{packageName}`, `{version}`, and `{installSpec}` placeholders of a configured self-update command. */
348: export function makeConfiguredSelfUpdateCommand(
349: 	argv: string[],
350: 	release: { packageName: string; version: string },
351: ): SelfUpdateCommand {
352: 	const values: Record<string, string> = {
353: 		packageName: release.packageName,
354: 		version: release.version,
355: 		installSpec: `${release.packageName}@${release.version}`,
356: 	};
357: 	const [command = "", ...args] = argv.map((arg) =>
358: 		arg.replace(/\{(packageName|version|installSpec)\}/g, (_, name: string) => values[name]),
359: 	);
360: 	return makeSelfUpdateCommandStep(command, args);
361: }
362:
363: export function getSelfUpdateUnavailableInstruction(
364: 	packageName: string,
365: 	npmCommand?: string[],
366: 	updatePackageTarget: SelfUpdatePackageTarget = packageName,
367: ): string {
368: 	const method = detectInstallMethod();
369: 	const target = normalizeSelfUpdatePackageTarget(updatePackageTarget);
370: 	if (method === "bun-binary") {
371: 		return `Download from: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/releases/latest`;
372: 	}
373: 	const command = getSelfUpdateCommandForMethod(method, packageName, target, npmCommand);
374: 	// Path-based detection also matches installs that only live under a package manager's directory,
375: 	// such as a wrapper under PNPM_HOME, so name the package manager only when it owns the install.
376: 	if (command && isManagedByGlobalPackageManager(method, packageName, npmCommand) && !isSelfUpdatePathWritable()) {
377: 		return `This installation is managed by a global ${method} install, but the install path is not writable. Update it yourself with: ${command.display}`;
378: 	}
379: 	return `Update ${target.installSpec} using the package manager, wrapper, or source checkout that provides this installation.`;
380: }
381:
382: export function getUpdateInstruction(packageName: string): string {
383: 	const method = detectInstallMethod();
384: 	const command = getSelfUpdateCommandForMethod(method, packageName);
385: 	if (command) {
386: 		return `Run: ${command.display}`;
387: 	}
388: 	return getSelfUpdateUnavailableInstruction(packageName);
389: }

391: // =============================================================================
392: // Package Asset Paths (shipped with executable)

395: /**
396:  * Get the base directory for resolving package assets (themes, package.json, README.md, CHANGELOG.md).
397:  * - For Bun binary: returns the directory containing the executable
398:  * - For Node.js: returns the package root containing package.json
399:  * - Ignores Bun binary metadata copied into dist/ when the package root is available
400:  */
401: export function findNodePackageDir(startDir: string): string {
402: 	let dir = startDir;
403: 	while (dir !== dirname(dir)) {
404: 		if (existsSync(join(dir, "package.json"))) {
405: 			const parent = dirname(dir);
406: 			// build:binary places Bun's metadata inside dist/. Node still needs the
407: 			// package root so its dist-relative asset paths do not become dist/dist/.
408: 			if (basename(dir) === "dist" && existsSync(join(parent, "package.json"))) {
409: 				return parent;
410: 			}
411: 			return dir;
412: 		}
413: 		dir = dirname(dir);
414: 	}
415: 	return startDir;
416: }
417:
418: export function getPackageDir(): string {
419: 	// Allow override via environment variable (useful for Nix/Guix where store paths tokenize poorly)
420: 	const envDir = process.env.PI_PACKAGE_DIR;
421: 	if (envDir) {
422: 		return normalizePath(envDir);
423: 	}
424:
425: 	if (isBunBinary) {
426: 		// Bun binary: process.execPath points to the compiled executable
427: 		return dirname(process.execPath);
428: 	}
429: 	return findNodePackageDir(__dirname);
430: }

524: /** Resolve the codemode worker entry for a release runtime. */
525: export function resolveCodemodeWorkerSpecifier(
526: 	runtime: "bun-binary" | "bundled-node" | "unbundled",
527: 	moduleUrl: string,
528: ): string | URL | undefined {
529: 	// Bun embeds explicit source entrypoints, but on Windows Bun 1.3 cannot map an absolute
530: 	// B:\~BUN URL back to one. A relative string with the original source extension works on
531: 	// every Bun platform.
532: 	if (runtime === "bun-binary") return "./src/extensions/codemode/worker.ts";
533: 	if (runtime === "bundled-node") return new URL("./codemode-worker.js", moduleUrl);
534: 	return undefined;
535: }
536:
537: let codemodeWorkerDataUrl: URL | undefined;
538:
539: /**
540:  * Get the codemode worker entry, or undefined to use the worker that ships next to pi-codemode.
541:  * The Bun and Node release builds both pass the worker as an extra entrypoint.
542:  */
543: export function getCodemodeWorkerSpecifier(): string | URL | undefined {
544: 	const runtime = isBunBinary ? "bun-binary" : isBundledNode ? "bundled-node" : "unbundled";
545: 	const specifier = resolveCodemodeWorkerSpecifier(runtime, import.meta.url);
546: 	if (runtime !== "bundled-node" || !(specifier instanceof URL)) return specifier;
547: 	// Spawn workers from an in-memory copy. An update replaces or deletes the file while this
548: 	// process keeps running (#10439). The bundle build keeps the worker free of relative imports
549: 	// and import.meta, so it runs from a data: URL.
550: 	codemodeWorkerDataUrl ??= new URL(`data:text/javascript;base64,${readFileSync(specifier).toString("base64")}`);
551: 	return codemodeWorkerDataUrl;
552: }
553:
554: export type InstallChange = { kind: "updated"; version: string } | { kind: "removed" };
555:
556: /**
557:  * Detect that the package this process runs from changed on disk, for example after `pi update`
558:  * in another terminal. Code loaded on demand can then be missing or from another version.
559:  *
560:  * Checks the package.json read at startup. Resolving it again would walk up past a deleted install
561:  * and could find an unrelated package.json, such as one in the home directory.
562:  */
563: export function detectInstallChange(packageJsonPath = startupPackageJsonPath): InstallChange | undefined {
564: 	// The Bun binary embeds its code, so replacing the executable does not affect this process.
565: 	if (isBunBinary || !packageJsonPath) return undefined;
566: 	let installed: PackageJson;
567: 	try {
568: 		installed = JSON.parse(stripBom(readFileSync(packageJsonPath, "utf-8"))) as PackageJson;
569: 	} catch (error) {
570: 		return (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT" ? { kind: "removed" } : undefined;
571: 	}
572: 	return installed.version && installed.version !== VERSION
573: 		? { kind: "updated", version: installed.version }
574: 		: undefined;
575: }
576:
577: // =============================================================================
578: // App Config (from package.json piConfig)
579: // =============================================================================
580:
581: interface PackageJson {
582: 	name?: string;
583: 	version?: string;
584: 	piConfig?: {
585: 		name?: string;
586: 		configDir?: string;
587: 	};
588: }
589:
590: let pkg: PackageJson = {};
591: /** The package.json this process started from, if one existed. */
592: let startupPackageJsonPath: string | undefined;
593: try {
594: 	const packageJsonPath = getPackageJsonPath();
595: 	pkg = JSON.parse(stripBom(readFileSync(packageJsonPath, "utf-8"))) as PackageJson;
596: 	startupPackageJsonPath = packageJsonPath;
597: } catch (e: unknown) {
598: 	const err = e as NodeJS.ErrnoException;
599: 	if (err.code !== "ENOENT") throw e;
600: }

605: export const APP_TITLE: string = piConfigName ? APP_NAME : "π";

607: export const VERSION: string = pkg.version || "0.0.0";

611: export const ENV_SESSION_DIR = `${APP_NAME.toUpperCase()}_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`;

61:
62: Commands are JSON objects written to stdin. Responses and events are JSON objects written to stdout. Every record occupies one line.
63:
64: Add an `id` to commands that need correlation. The matching response repeats that ID. Events generally have no command ID because they describe session activity rather than one request.
65:
66: A successful `prompt` response means the prompt was accepted, queued, or handled. It does not mean the run completed. Continue consuming events through `agent_settled` when completion matters.
67:
68: RPC commands can change models, inspect state, manage sessions, run shell commands, and answer extension UI requests.
69:
70: Extension dialogs form a request-response subprotocol. Other extension UI updates are notifications that a client may display or ignore. TUI-only extension capabilities are unavailable or degraded outside interactive mode.
71:
72: For Node.js or TypeScript integrations, prefer `RpcClient` from `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`. It starts a Pi RPC child process, correlates requests, exposes typed command methods, and delivers session events to listeners.
73:
74: The [RPC client example](../examples/rpc-client.ts) sends one prompt, streams text and tool activity, waits for `agent_settled`, and shuts down the child process. It is included in the repository’s TypeScript checks.
75:
76: `RpcClient.promptAndWait()` installs its event listener before sending the prompt, avoiding a race with fast completions. For separate operations, subscribe before calling `prompt()` and call `waitForIdle()` only while a run is active.
77:
78: The client requires a path to a runnable Pi CLI. The repository example points at `dist/cli.js`, so the package must be built before that example runs from a checkout.
79:
80: If you are building a client without `RpcClient`, start with [RPC Protocol](rpc.md), then use [RPC Commands](rpc-commands.md) and [JSON Event Stream](json.md) as the wire references.

1: # Development Rules
2:
3: ## Conversational Style
4:
5: - Keep answers short and concise
6: - No emojis in commits, issues, PR comments, or code
7: - No fluff or cheerful filler text (e.g., "Thanks @user" not "Thanks so much @user!")
8: - Technical prose only, be direct
9: - Use concise, clear, simple language. Define unavoidable jargon before using it.
10: - Explain non-trivial designs and problems as: problem, concrete example or short trace, then solution. State why the solution is necessary and distinguish it from optional complexity.
11: - Prefer concrete behavior and small illustrations over abstract summaries, dense terminology, or unexplained lists of changes.
12: - When the user asks a question, answer it first before making edits or running implementation commands.
13: - When responding to user feedback or an analysis, explicitly say whether you agree or disagree before saying what you changed.

15: ## Code Quality
16:
17: - Read files in full before wide-ranging changes, before editing files you have not fully inspected, and when asked to investigate or audit. Do not rely on search snippets for broad changes.
18: - No `any` unless absolutely necessary.
19: - No runtime checks of values whose types TypeScript already guarantees (no `typeof`/`instanceof`/`Array.isArray`/shape guards on typed parameters, typed callback results or typed declarations). Validate only at decided trust boundaries (wire input, schema-checked arguments and params).
20: - Inline single-line helpers that have only one call site.
21: - Check node_modules for external API types; don't guess.
22: - **No inline imports** (`await import()`, `import("pkg").Type`, dynamic type imports). Top-level imports only.
23: - In `packages/coding-agent`, resolve package assets through helpers in `src/config.ts`. Do not use `__dirname` directly; the helpers account for source checkouts, npm installations, and standalone binaries.
24: - Never remove or downgrade code to fix type errors from outdated deps; upgrade the dep instead.
25: - Use only erasable TypeScript syntax (Node strip-only mode) in code checked by the root config (`packages/*/src`, `packages/*/test`, `packages/coding-agent/examples`): no parameter properties, `enum`, `namespace`/`module`, `import =`, `export =`, or other constructs needing JS emit. Use explicit fields with constructor assignments.
26: - Always ask before removing functionality or code that appears intentional.
27: - Do not preserve backward compatibility unless the user asks for it.
28: - Never hardcode key checks (e.g. `matchesKey(keyData, "ctrl+x")`). Add defaults to `DEFAULT_EDITOR_KEYBINDINGS` or `DEFAULT_APP_KEYBINDINGS` so they stay configurable.
29: - Never modify `packages/ai/src/models.generated.ts` directly; update the catalog definitions in `packages/ai/catalog/` instead (see its README), then regenerate. Including the resulting `models.generated.ts` diff is always OK, even if regeneration includes unrelated upstream model metadata changes. The generated model data in `packages/ai/src/providers/data/` is gitignored: never stage it, and don't look for it in git history.
30:
31: ## Chord v2 Code Style
32:
33: Binding for Chord v2 (`packages/chord/src/`) and its tests, when writing and when reviewing. The model is pi-durable's source.
34:
35: - Files: one concept per file, named after it; no one-helper files, no grab-bag files. First line: a comment saying what the file is for. Order: imports, exported types, then the public entry point first and its helpers below it in the order they are used; constants right above their first user. A blank line between top-level declarations. Split files by concept, never by size: one concept may take a long file (up to about 1,000 lines is fine); a second concept in a file is the reason to split.
36: - Functions: every export has a one-line doc comment saying what it does or guarantees. Inline comments explain a non-obvious why (cost, race, decided rule), never what the next line does. Short functions with one job (about 40 lines needs a reason; one `switch` over a tagged union is fine). No boolean flag parameters that switch behaviour: two functions or a tagged value. Never write the same lines twice. Context last: required args, then `context`/`ctx` (always required, as in Durable; optional only on error-reporting paths), then optional args.
37: - Types and checks: tagged unions for every state and result. Casts only where TypeScript cannot express a decided invariant, each with a short why. Every remaining runtime check names the trust boundary it serves (wire input, schema-checked params and arguments, declaration policy the types cannot express). Same-host values are plain data, immutable by convention: never copied, frozen or walked to enforce it; freeze only Chord-owned metadata when a decision says so. No defensive code against broken adapters, callers or our own modules.
38: - Cost and memory: no hot-path work a decision did not ask for (walks, copies, compilations, per-call allocations). The function doing counted work counts it through its context; call sites never count for others. Caches are `WeakMap`s keyed by their owner, each with a GC test; no module-level strong caches.
39: - Names and API: the design's vocabulary (`params`, `binding`, `principal key`), no invented synonyms; decided `ChordError` codes and reasons. Export only what a later layer or app needs. No dev or test modes, no unrequested options.
40: - Tests: one test file per source file, one `describe` per mechanism, the layer spec's test list case by case; cost guards through the in-memory telemetry adapter; GC tests for every cache and binding. Every slice also adds one or more runnable examples in `packages/chord/test/examples/NN-topic.ts`, one topic each, numbered across slices, written as references for Chord's users (Durable's `test/examples/` format: header with what it shows and how to run it, commented steps, printed results).
41: - Slices: Chord v2 is built in vertical slices (`packages/chord/docs/slices.md`). Implementers and reviewers read the slice spec, the feature map in `slices.md` and the whole of `packages/chord/docs/design.md` in full, and check the work against all three; slice specs cite design sections for orientation, not as a reading limit.
42: - Deferred work: anything left to a later slice goes into the section "Carry-over" of `packages/chord/docs/slices.md` under that slice, in the same change; a slice's spec and build include every entry of its section.
43: - Before reporting: re-read every changed file top to bottom as a stranger would; each file must be understandable without jumping around. Then `npm run check` and the layer's tests.

47: - After code changes (not docs): `npm run check` (full output, no tail). Fix all errors, warnings, and infos before committing. Does not run tests.

61:

## Sections and what problem each solves

**Conversational Style (3-13)** — output shape. Short answers, no emojis, no filler, jargon defined before use. Two behavioral rules matter most: answer a question *before* editing files, and say agree/disagree explicitly before describing changes you made.

**Code Quality (15-29)** — TypeScript discipline. The recurring theme is "the type system is the contract, so stop re-checking it": no `typeof`/`instanceof`/`Array.isArray` guards on values TS already types — runtime checks only at real trust boundaries (wire input, schema-validated args). Also: read files in full before wide changes, no inline `await import()`, no `any`, only erasable TS syntax (no `enum`/`namespace`/parameter properties) because the code runs under Node's strip-only mode. `packages/ai/src/models.generated.ts` is generated — edit `packages/ai/catalog/` instead.

**Chord v2 Code Style (31-43)** — a second, stricter rule set that only binds `packages/chord/src/` and its tests. One concept per file named after the concept; tagged unions for all state; no defensive code against our own modules; no hot-path work no decision asked for; caches must be `WeakMap`s with a GC test; every slice adds a runnable example in `packages/chord/test/examples/NN-topic.ts`. It also fixes the workflow: work proceeds as vertical slices defined in `packages/chord/docs/slices.md`, and unfinished work goes in that file's "Carry-over" section in the same change.

**Commands (45-58)** — the operational detail most likely to bite. `npm run check` is the verify step (lint + typecheck, no tests); `npm run build` only when something needs `dist/`; never run `npm test` or the raw vitest suite, because e2e tests self-activate when provider endpoint/auth env vars are present and would burn real API calls. Run `./test.sh` or a single file instead. Tests under `packages/coding-agent/test/suite/` must use `test/suite/harness.ts` and the faux provider — no real keys. Ad-hoc scripts go in a temp file, not inline bash (which is why I wrote `/tmp/opencode/check-config-dir.ts` earlier instead of a heredoc).

**Dependency and Install Security (60-67)** — supply-chain policy: `package-lock.json` is treated as reviewed code, installs use `--ignore-scripts`, a pre-commit hook blocks lockfile commits unless `PI_ALLOW_LOCKFILE_CHANGE=1`.

**Git (69-89)** — the reason is stated in the file: several agent sessions share this working directory at once, so any command that touches files you didn't change destroys another session's work. Hence: stage explicit paths, never `git add -A`, never `git reset --hard`/`git stash`/`git clean -fd`/`--no-verify`, never force push, and abort rebase conflicts in files you didn't touch.

**Issues and PRs (91-113)** — inspect PRs without checking them out (`gh pr diff`, `git show <ref>:<path>`); label issues `pkg:*`; post comments from a temp file with `--body-file` and end them with an AI-generated disclaimer.

**Changelog (119-134)** — one `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` per package, new entries only under `## [Unreleased]`, released version sections immutable.

**Releasing (136)** and **tmux testing (115)** — stubs that defer to skills: `.pi/skills/release.md` and `.pi/skills/interactive-testing.md`.

**User Override (140)** — if your instruction conflicts with a rule above, the agent must ask for confirmation first rather than silently picking one.

```ts
render(width: number): string[] {
	return this.hasSessionEntries() ? [] : this.tip.render(width);
}
```

and `interactive-mode.ts:647` supplies the predicate:

```ts
this.tipContainer.addChild(new SessionTip(() => this.sessionManager.getEntryCount() > 0));
```

The intent is "show the tip only on a blank launch screen." The predicate is raw session-entry count, and a *new* session is never at zero.

## Trace

I ran `./toucan-test.sh` in a pty (80x24) with an empty agent dir (`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/tmp/opencode/fresh-agent`) and cwd `/tmp/opencode`, so no sessions and no settings existed. Startup still printed `Welcome back!` and no tip. A throwaway extension hooked `session_start` and dumped the session:

```
session_start: count=1 types=["thinking_level_change"]
```

One entry, already present at `session_start`. `setThinkingLevel` (`agent-session.ts:2746`) appends whenever the level differs from the previous state, and startup applies the default level, so a brand-new session gets a `thinking_level_change` before the first render. `getEntryCount()` returns `byId.size` (`session-manager.ts:1522`), which excludes only the header, so that one metadata entry makes the predicate true forever. Same bug explains why the launch panel always says "Welcome back!" (`interactive-mode.ts:1051` uses the same expression).

Nothing you renamed is involved. `test/launch-layout.test.ts` passes because its fake session hardcodes `getEntryCount: () => 0` (`test/launch-layout.test.ts:28`), which is exactly the state production never reaches.

## Two ways to fix it, and they differ in what "fresh session" means

1. **Change the predicate to conversation content.** A session is "started" when it has a `message` entry, not when it has metadata. Add something like `hasMessages()` to `SessionManager` and use it at `interactive-mode.ts:647` and `:1051`. Tip behaves as documented: visible on launch, hidden after the first prompt, back after `/new`. Local to the launch UI.

2. **Stop appending the startup `thinking_level_change` on an empty session.** The selection would be recorded only once the conversation exists. This fixes the count at the source but changes what goes into session files, and `getBranchSelection`/resume logic reads those entries — it needs the session-format reasoning checked against tree navigation and resume. Wider blast radius.

I'd take 1, and also make `launch-layout.test.ts` drive a real `SessionManager` for the fresh case so the mock's `() => 0` can't hide this again.

Which one do you want?

If no alias, pick the latest dated version\n */\nasync function resolveModelScope(\n\tpatterns: string[],\n): Promise<Array<{ model: Model<Api>; thinkingLevel: ThinkingLevel }>> {\n\tconst { models: availableModels, error } = await getAvailableModels();\n\n\tif (error) {\n\t\tconsole.warn(chalk.yellow(`Warning: Error loading models: ${error}`));\n\t\treturn [];\n\t}\n\n\tconst scopedModels: Array<{ model: Model<Api>; thinkingLevel: ThinkingLevel }> = [];\n\n\tfor (const pattern of patterns) {\n\t\t// Parse pattern:level format\n\t\tconst parts = pattern.split(\":\");\n\t\tconst modelPattern = parts[0];\n\t\tlet thinkingLevel: ThinkingLevel = \"off\";\n\n\t\tif (parts.length > 1) {\n\t\t\tconst level = parts[1];\n\t\t\tif (\n\t\t\t\tlevel === \"off\" ||\n\t\t\t\tlevel === \"minimal\" ||\n\t\t\t\tlevel === \"low\" ||\n\t\t\t\tlevel === \"medium\" ||\n\t\t\t\tlevel === \"high\" ||\n\t\t\t\tlevel === \"xhigh\"\n\t\t\t) {\n\t\t\t\tthinkingLevel = level;\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tconsole.warn(\n\t\t\t\t\tchalk.yellow(`Warning: Invalid thinking level \"${level}\" in pattern \"${pattern}\". {\n\t\t\t// Prefer alias - if multiple aliases, pick the one that sorts highest\n\t\t\taliases.sort((a, b) => b.id.localeCompare(a.id));\n\t\t\tbestMatch = aliases[0];\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t// No alias 	private constructor(

		newSessionOptions?: NewSessionOptions,
		preloadedFileEntries?: FileEntry[],
	) {
		this.cwd = resolvePath(cwd);

		this.persist = persist;

		}

		} else if (preloadedFileEntries?.length) {
			this._loadEntries(preloadedFileEntries, newSessionOptions);
		} else {

		}
	}

/** A single startup tip shown directly above the input box for the whole session. */

import { type Component, visibleWidth } from "@hyzek/toucan-tui";
import { APP_NAME } from "../../../config.ts";
import { theme } from "../theme/theme.ts";

/** Startup tips, chosen at random for each launch. Keep these to slash commands and @file syntax: key names live in the keybinding config, not here. */
const TIPS = [
	"Tip: Use /new for a fresh context for fresh tasks.",
	"Tip: Reference files with @path, or drop them into the terminal.",
	"Tip: Start a line with ! to run bash, !! to run it without context.",
	"Tip: /model switches models and /settings opens configuration.",
	`Tip: ${APP_NAME} can explain its own features and look up its docs. Ask it how to use or extend ${APP_NAME}.`,
];

export function pickLaunchTip(): string {
	return TIPS[Math.floor(Math.random() * TIPS.length)]!;
}

export class TipLine implements Component {
	private readonly tip: string;

	constructor(tip: string) {
		this.tip = tip;
	}

	invalidate(): void {}

	render(width: number): string[] {
		const text = theme.fg("dim", this.tip);
		const padding = " ".repeat(Math.max(1, width - visibleWidth(text) - 1));
		return [`${padding}${text}`];
	}
}

/**
 * The launch tip, visible only while the session has no user or assistant message. Once the
 * session has started it renders nothing, and it comes back after /new because the new session
 * starts blank. A fresh launch already holds model and thinking-level entries, so entry count
 * is not the test.
 */
export class SessionTip implements Component {
	private readonly tip = new TipLine(pickLaunchTip());
	private readonly hasConversation: () => boolean;

	constructor(hasConversation: () => boolean) {
		this.hasConversation = hasConversation;
	}

	invalidate(): void {}

	render(width: number): string[] {
		return this.hasConversation() ? [] : this.tip.render(width);
	}
}

	/**
	 * Whether the session holds a user or assistant message, as opposed to only setup entries.

```ts
	render(width: number): string[] {
		const state = this.session.state;
		const branch = this.footerData.getGitBranch();
		const sessionName = this.session.sessionManager.getSessionName();
		const directory = formatCwdForFooter(this.session.sessionManager.getCwd(), homedir());

		// Model and thinking level lead the bar, indented one cell to line up under the input
		// caret, then branch, session name, and the working directory.
		const modelName = state.model?.id || "no-model";
		let left = modelName;
		if (state.model?.reasoning) {
			const thinkingLevel = state.thinkingLevel || "off";
			left = thinkingLevel === "off" ? `${modelName} • thinking off` : `${modelName} • ${thinkingLevel}`;
		}

		const routed = this.session.routedModel;

			const level = routed.thinkingLevel ? ` • ${routed.thinkingLevel}` : "";
			left += ` → ${routed.model.id}${level}`;

			left = `${left} (${branch})`;
		}
		if (sessionName) {
			left = `${left} • ${sessionName}`;

		const indent = " ".repeat(visibleWidth(INPUT_PROMPT));

=== footer.ts head/render ===
import { homedir } from "node:os";
import { isAbsolute, relative, resolve, sep } from "node:path";
import { type Component, truncateToWidth, visibleWidth } from "@hyzek/toucan-tui";
import type { AgentSession } from "../../../core/agent-session.ts";
import { areExperimentalFeaturesEnabled } from "../../../core/experimental.ts";
import type { ReadonlyFooterDataProvider } from "../../../core/footer-data-provider.ts";
import { theme } from "../theme/theme.ts";
import { INPUT_PROMPT } from "./custom-editor.ts";

/**
 * Sanitize text for display in a single-line status.
 * Removes newlines, tabs, carriage returns, and other control characters.
 */
function sanitizeStatusText(text: string): string {
	// Replace newlines, tabs, carriage returns with space, then collapse multiple spaces
	return text
		.replace(/[\r\n\t]/g, " ")
		.replace(/ +/g, " ")
		.trim();
}

/**
 * Format token counts for compact footer display.
 */
export function formatTokens(count: number): string {
	if (count < 1000) return count.toString();
	if (count < 10000) return `${(count / 1000).toFixed(1)}k`;
	if (count < 1000000) return `${Math.round(count / 1000)}k`;
	if (count < 10000000) return `${(count / 1000000).toFixed(1)}M`;
	return `${Math.round(count / 1000000)}M`;
}

export function formatCwdForFooter(cwd: string, home: string | undefined): string {
	if (!home) return cwd;

	const resolvedCwd = resolve(cwd);
	const resolvedHome = resolve(home);
	const relativeToHome = relative(resolvedHome, resolvedCwd);
	const isInsideHome =
		relativeToHome === "" ||
		(relativeToHome !== ".." && !relativeToHome.startsWith(`..${sep}`) && !isAbsolute(relativeToHome));

	if (!isInsideHome) return cwd;
	return relativeToHome === "" ? "~" : `~${sep}${relativeToHome}`;
}

/**
 * Footer bar showing model and thinking level, git branch, session name, and the working
 * directory. Git branch and extension statuses come from the provider.
 */

## 2. Mounting: statusContainer vs. embedded in the input band

`StatusIndicator` (`src/modes/interactive/components/status-indicator.ts`) exposes the two border hooks:
```ts
renderInBorder(width)        // 24-27: super.render(width + 2)[1], strip leading space, truncate
renderSpinnerInBorder(width) // 29-31: truncateToWidth(this.getRenderedIndicator(), ...)
```
(`Loader.render` prepends a blank line — `packages/tui/src/components/loader.ts:43-45` — hence the `[1]` index.)

The only consumer is `CustomEditor.renderTopBorder` (`src/modes/interactive/components/custom-editor.ts:60-104`):
- `renderInBorder(Math.max(1, width - 5))` at line 65; fallback `renderSpinnerInBorder(width)` when the overflow label doesn't fit (77) or the label is too wide (96).
- With `borders: false` (the input band): `if (!this.borders) return truncateToWidth(` ${status}`, width, "")` (line 68) — the status becomes a plain text line.
- With borders: it composes `"── " + status + "─..."` centered with the `↑ N more` overflow label (81–103).

Where that line lands: `Editor.render` in `packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts` calls `const topBorder = this.renderTopBorder(width, this.scrollOffset); if (topBorder !== "") result.push(...)` (612–613) — it is the **first rendered line of the editor**, above the `minLines: 3` band rows padded around the text (607–619). The band config is `inputBandOptions()` (`custom-editor.ts:22-32`: `borders: false`, `prompt: "› "`, `minLines: 3`); the default editor is built with `embedWorkingStatus: true` at interactive-mode 639–644. When no indicator is set, `renderTopBorder` returns `""` and the line is omitted.

Routing rule (`showStatusIndicator`, 2088–2099): embedded in the editor border line whenever the active editor opts in; only otherwise added to `statusContainer`. `statusContainer` is mounted standalone in regular mode (`mountInteractiveTui(..., [.., this.statusContainer, this.editorContainer, ..]`, 991–1001) and, in fullscreen, sits in the dock above widgets/tip/editor in `createChatViewport` (`chat-viewport.ts:33-42`, `{ component: options.status, shrink: 1, minSize: 0 }` line 35; editor slot `minSize: 3` line 38).

## 4. Streaming updates and usage fields

Handlers: `message_start` for assistant role creates `this.streamingComponent` + `this.streamingMessage` (3266–3279); `message_update` (3282–3316) does `this.streamingMessage = event.message; this.streamingComponent.updateContent(this.streamingMessage, true)`; `message_end` finalizes (3318–3358). Events originate from `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts:424–451` — each streaming AI event re-emits `{ type: "message_update", assistantMessageEvent: event, message: { ...partialMessage } }` (shallow copy of the shared partial).

`AssistantMessage.usage` is a required field (`packages/ai/src/types.ts:606`). `Usage` (`types.ts:467–495`) exact fields:
```ts
input: number; output: number; cacheRead: number; cacheWrite: number;
cacheWrite1h?: number;   // subset of cacheWrite, Anthropic only
reasoning?: number;      // "subset of `output`... Set to a number (possibly 0) by
                         // providers that expose a reasoning breakdown; left undefined by providers that don't."
totalTokens: number;
cost: { input; output; cacheRead; cacheWrite; total; totalFromProvider? };
```
During streaming, the partial starts with zeroed usage and **no** `reasoning` key (`packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts:327–334`); usage is replaced as soon as a chunk carries it (`output.usage = parseChunkUsage(chunk.usage, model)` 554–555, with `stream_options.include_usage` at 827; `reasoning: rawUsage.completion_tokens_details?.reasoning_tokens || 0` at 1552). Anthropic updates partial usage mid-stream on each `message_delta` (`anthropic-messages.ts:1097–1126`), including `output.usage.reasoning = thinkingTokens` from `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` (1118–1121) and computed `totalTokens` (1124–1125). OpenAI Responses sets `reasoning: response.usage.output_tokens_details?.reasoning_tokens || 0` (`openai-responses-shared.ts:644`); Google sets `reasoning: chunk.usageMetadata.thoughtsTokenCount || 0` (`google-generative-ai.ts:240`, `google-vertex.ts:255`). So yes — a reasoning/thinking token count exists (`usage.reasoning`) and is populated on the streaming partial wherever the provider reports it; it is included in `output`, and interactive-mode already reads message usage at `message_end` (`maybeShowCacheMissNotice(this.streamingMessage)` 3351).

## 5. `Loader` in packages/tui

`packages/tui/src/components/loader.ts`:
- Signature (28–41): `constructor(ui: TUI, spinnerColorFn: (str: string) => string, messageColorFn: (str: string) => string, message: string = "Loading...", indicator?: LoaderIndicatorOptions)`; extends `Text` (`super("", 1, 0)`).
- Animation: `DEFAULT_FRAMES = ["⠋","⠙","⠹","⠸","⠼","⠴","⠦","⠧","⠇","⠏"]` (11), `DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS = 80` (12); `restartAnimation` (77–86) runs `setInterval(() => { currentFrame++; updateDisplay(); }, this.intervalMs)` — one tick advances the frame and re-renders. `setIndicator` (69–75) resets frames/interval and calls `start()` (which calls `updateDisplay` + `restartAnimation`); an empty `frames` array hides the indicator (79–80); custom frames render verbatim without spinner color (`renderIndicatorVerbatim`, 70, 88–91).
- `setMessage(message)` (59–62): stores `this.message` and calls `updateDisplay()`, which does `this.setText(`${indicator}${this.messageColorFn(this.message)}`)` plus `this.ui.requestRender()` (93–100). `invalidate()` also re-runs `updateDisplay` (64–67).
- In-place text changes by subclasses: yes, no component recreation needed. Proof in-repo: `RetryStatusIndicator` calls `this.setMessage(retryMessage(seconds))` from a `CountdownTimer` tick (`status-indicator.ts:64–73`; `CountdownTimer` ticks each 1000 ms, `countdown-timer.ts:21–30`), and the extension API `setWorkingMessage` calls `activeStatusIndicator.setMessage(...)` (interactive-mode 2419–2421). Disposal: `StatusIndicator.dispose()` → `this.stop()` (status-indicator.ts:33–35), clearing the interval (loader.ts:52–57).

149: 	(timer as any)?.unref?.();
150: }
151:
152: function stopLoaderIfUiStopped(loader: any): boolean {
153: 	if (!loader?.ui || !(loader.ui as any).stopped) return false;
154: 	loader.stop?.();
155: 	return true;
156: }
157:
158: (Loader.prototype as any).updateDisplay = function patchedUpdateDisplay() {
159: 	if (stopLoaderIfUiStopped(this)) return;
160: 	const frame = OB_FRAMES[this.currentFrame % OB_FRAMES.length];
161: 	const message = typeof this.message === "string" && RAW_ANSI_RE.test(this.message)
162: 		? this.message
163: 		: this.messageColorFn(this.message);
164: 	const nextText = `${this.spinnerColorFn(frame)} ${message}`;
165: 	if ((this as any)[LOADER_LAST_TEXT] === nextText) return;
166: 	(this as any)[LOADER_LAST_TEXT] = nextText;
167: 	this.setText(nextText);
168: 	if (this.ui && !(this.ui as any).stopped) {
169: 		(globalThis as any)[ACTIVE_UI_SYMBOL] = this.ui;
170: 		this.ui.requestRender();
171: 	}
172: };
173:
174: Loader.prototype.start = function patchedStart() {
175: 	this.stop();
176: 	(this as any)[LOADER_ACTIVE] = true;
177: 	const generation = ((this as any)[LOADER_GENERATION] ?? 0) + 1;
178: 	(this as any)[LOADER_GENERATION] = generation;
179: 	delete (this as any)[LOADER_LAST_TEXT];
180: 	(this as any).updateDisplay();
181: 	if (OB_FRAMES.length <= 1 || stopLoaderIfUiStopped(this)) return;
182: 	const scheduleNext = () => {
183: 		if ((this as any)[LOADER_ACTIVE] !== true || (this as any)[LOADER_GENERATION] !== generation || stopLoaderIfUiStopped(this)) return;
184: 		const intervalMs = getLoaderIntervalMs(this);
185: 		const timer = setTimeout(() => {
186: 			(this as any).intervalId = null;
187: 			if ((this as any)[LOADER_ACTIVE] !== true || (this as any)[LOADER_GENERATION] !== generation || stopLoaderIfUiStopped(this)) return;
188: 			(this as any).currentFrame = ((this as any).currentFrame + 1) % OB_FRAMES.length;
189: 			(this as any).updateDisplay();
190: 			scheduleNext();
191: 		}, intervalMs);
192: 		unrefTimer(timer);
193: 		(this as any).intervalId = timer;
194: 	};
195: 	scheduleNext();
196: };
197:
198: Loader.prototype.stop = function patchedStop() {
199: 	(this as any)[LOADER_ACTIVE] = false;
200: 	(this as any)[LOADER_GENERATION] = ((this as any)[LOADER_GENERATION] ?? 0) + 1;
201: 	if ((this as any).intervalId) {
202: 		clearTimeout((this as any).intervalId);
203: 		(this as any).intervalId = null;
204: 	}
205: };

478: /** Format elapsed ms as compact duration: 5s, 1m 23s, 1h 2m 3s */
479: // What a running tool is doing, for the working line ("Running npm test…",
480: // "Reading stats.py…"). Random verbs stay for the time the model is thinking.
481: // No ellipsis of its own: the working line already ends in "…".
482: function clip(text: string, max: number): string {
483: 	const oneLine = text.split("\n")[0]?.trim() ?? "";
484: 	return oneLine.length > max ? oneLine.slice(0, max).trimEnd() : oneLine;
485: }
486:
487: function humanizeToolName(name: string): string {
488: 	const direct = /^mcp__.+?__(.+)$/.exec(name);
489: 	return (direct ? direct[1] : name)
490: 		.replace(/([a-z0-9])([A-Z])/g, "$1 $2")
491: 		.replace(/[_-]+/g, " ")
492: 		.replace(/\b\w/g, (char) => char.toUpperCase());
493: }
494:
495: export function describeToolActivity(name: string, args: any): string {
496: 	const str = (...keys: string[]): string => {
497: 		for (const key of keys) {
498: 			const value = args?.[key];
499: 			if (typeof value === "string" && value.trim()) return value.trim();
500: 		}
501: 		return "";
502: 	};
503: 	const file = basename(str("path", "file_path"));
504: 	switch (name) {
505: 		case "bash": {
506: 			const command = clip(str("command"), 50);
507: 			return command ? `Running ${command}` : "Running a shell command";
508: 		}
509: 		case "read":
510: 			return file ? `Reading ${file}` : "Reading a file";
511: 		case "edit":
512: 			return file ? `Editing ${file}` : "Editing a file";
513: 		case "write":
514: 			return file ? `Writing ${file}` : "Writing a file";
515: 		case "grep":
516: 		case "find": {
517: 			const pattern = clip(str("pattern"), 40);
518: 			return pattern ? `Searching for ${pattern}` : "Searching";
519: 		}
520: 		case "ls":
521: 			return `Listing ${str("path") || "."}`;
522: 		case "Agent": {
523: 			const description = clip(str("description"), 50);
524: 			return description ? `Waiting for agent: ${description}` : "Waiting for an agent";
525: 		}
526: 		case "ask_user_question":
527: 		case "questionnaire":
528: 		case "question":
529: 			return "Waiting for your answer";
530: 		default:
531: 			return `Running ${humanizeToolName(name)}`;
532: 	}
533: }
534:
535: function formatDuration(ms: number): string {
536: 	const totalSec = Math.floor(ms / 1000);
537: 	const h = Math.floor(totalSec / 3600);
538: 	const m = Math.floor((totalSec % 3600) / 60);
539: 	const s = totalSec % 60;
540: 	if (h > 0) return `${h}h ${m}m ${s}s`;
541: 	if (m > 0) return `${m}m ${s}s`;
542: 	return `${s}s`;
543: }
544:
545: function formatCount(value: number): string {
546: 	return new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US").format(value);
547: }
548:
549: /** Characters the model produced in one content block: text, thinking, or tool-call arguments. */
550: function contentBlockLength(block: any): number {
551: 	if (block?.type === "text" && typeof block.text === "string") return block.text.length;
552: 	if (block?.type === "thinking" && typeof block.thinking === "string") return block.thinking.length;
553: 	if (block?.type === "toolCall") {
554: 		try {
555: 			return JSON.stringify(block.arguments ?? {}).length;
556: 		} catch {
557: 			return 0;
558: 		}
559: 	}
560: 	return 0;
561: }
562:
563: /** Output tokens of a finished assistant message: the provider's count, or an estimate (chars / 4). */
564: function messageOutputTokens(message: any): number {
565: 	const reported = message?.usage?.output;
566: 	if (typeof reported === "number" && Number.isFinite(reported) && reported > 0) return reported;
567: 	if (!Array.isArray(message?.content)) return 0;
568: 	return Math.round(message.content.reduce((sum: number, block: any) => sum + contentBlockLength(block), 0) / 4);
569: }

571: function statusText(text: string): string {
572: 	return `${STATUS_DIM}${text}${RESET}`;
573: }
574:
575: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
576: // Herdr lifecycle reporting
577: //
578: // Stock herdr pi screen detection only matches the literal "Working...".
579: // This extension replaces that text with themed spinner verbs (Cooking…,
580: // Syncing…, …), so herdr sidebars go idle/stale while pi is actually busy.
581: // When running inside herdr (HERDR_ENV=1), report working/idle over the
582: // socket only when herdr's official pi integration is not installed. The
583: // official integration owns the same lifecycle authority and must remain the
584: // sole reporter when present. UI is unchanged.
585: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
586:
587: type HerdrAgentState = "working" | "idle";
588:
589: const HERDR_ENV = process.env.HERDR_ENV;
590: const HERDR_SOCKET_PATH = process.env.HERDR_SOCKET_PATH;
591: const HERDR_SOCKET_ENDPOINT =
592: 	process.platform === "win32" && HERDR_SOCKET_PATH
593: 		? `\\\\.\\pipe\\${HERDR_SOCKET_PATH}`
594: 		: HERDR_SOCKET_PATH;
595: const HERDR_PANE_ID = process.env.HERDR_PANE_ID;
596: // Must be exactly "herdr:pi" — herdr only grants full lifecycle authority
597: // (skip screen-manifest fallback) to that official source pair with agent "pi".
598: const HERDR_SOURCE = "herdr:pi";
599: const HERDR_INTEGRATION_MARKER = "HERDR_INTEGRATION_ID=pi";
600: let officialHerdrIntegrationInstalled: boolean | undefined;
601:
602: function hasOfficialHerdrIntegration(): boolean {
603: 	if (officialHerdrIntegrationInstalled !== undefined) {
604: 		return officialHerdrIntegrationInstalled;
605: 	}
606:
607: 	const agentDir = process.env.PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR
608: 		|| join(homedir(), ".pi", "agent");
609:
610: 	try {
611: 		const integrationPath = join(agentDir, "extensions", "herdr-agent-state.ts");
612: 		officialHerdrIntegrationInstalled =
613: 			existsSync(integrationPath)
614: 			&& readFileSync(integrationPath, "utf8").includes(HERDR_INTEGRATION_MARKER);
615: 	} catch {
616: 		officialHerdrIntegrationInstalled = false;
617: 	}
618: 	return officialHerdrIntegrationInstalled;
619: }
620:
621: function herdrEnabled(): boolean {
622: 	return HERDR_ENV === "1"
623: 		&& !!HERDR_SOCKET_PATH
624: 		&& !!HERDR_PANE_ID
625: 		&& !hasOfficialHerdrIntegration();
626: }
627:
628: function herdrSendAttempt(request: unknown, timeoutMs: number): Promise<boolean> {
629: 	if (!herdrEnabled()) return Promise.resolve(true);
630:
631: 	return new Promise((resolve) => {
632: 		let done = false;
633: 		let timeout: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
634: 		const finish = (delivered: boolean) => {
635: 			if (done) return;
636: 			done = true;
637: 			if (timeout) clearTimeout(timeout);
638: 			socket.destroy();
639: 			resolve(delivered);
640: 		};
641:
642: 		const socket = net.createConnection(HERDR_SOCKET_ENDPOINT!);
643: 		socket.on("error", () => finish(false));
644: 		socket.on("connect", () => socket.write(`${JSON.stringify(request)}\n`));
645: 		socket.on("data", () => finish(true));
646: 		socket.on("end", () => finish(false));
647: 		timeout = setTimeout(() => finish(false), timeoutMs);
648: 		unrefTimer(timeout);
649: 	});
650: }
651:
652: async function herdrSend(request: unknown): Promise<void> {
653: 	if (await herdrSendAttempt(request, 500)) return;
654: 	await herdrSendAttempt(request, 1500);
655: }
656:
657: let herdrReportSeq = Date.now() * 1000;
658: let herdrSessionId: string | undefined;
659: let herdrSessionPath: string | undefined;
660: let herdrSendInFlight = false;
661: let herdrQueued: { state: HerdrAgentState; seq: number } | undefined;
662: let herdrLastState: HerdrAgentState | undefined;
663:
664: function herdrNextSeq(): number {
665: 	herdrReportSeq += 1;
666: 	return herdrReportSeq;
667: }
668:
669: function herdrUpdateSessionRef(ctx: any): void {
670: 	try {
671: 		const file = ctx?.sessionManager?.getSessionFile?.();
672: 		herdrSessionPath =
673: 			typeof file === "string" && file.startsWith("/") ? file : undefined;
674: 	} catch {
675: 		herdrSessionPath = undefined;
676: 	}
677:
678: 	try {
679: 		const id = ctx?.sessionManager?.getSessionId?.();
680: 		herdrSessionId = typeof id === "string" && id.length > 0 ? id : undefined;
681: 	} catch {
682: 		herdrSessionId = undefined;
683: 	}
684: }
685:
686: function herdrWithSessionRef(params: Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown> {
687: 	if (herdrSessionPath) return { ...params, agent_session_path: herdrSessionPath };
688: 	if (herdrSessionId) return { ...params, agent_session_id: herdrSessionId };
689: 	return params;
690: }
691:
692: function herdrCurrentSessionRef(): Record<string, unknown> | undefined {
693: 	if (herdrSessionPath) return { agent_session_path: herdrSessionPath };
694: 	if (herdrSessionId) return { agent_session_id: herdrSessionId };
695: 	return undefined;
696: }
697:
698: function herdrReportSession(sessionStartSource?: string): Promise<void> {
699: 	const sessionRef = herdrCurrentSessionRef();
700: 	if (!sessionRef) return Promise.resolve();
701:
702: 	return herdrSend({
703: 		id: `${HERDR_SOURCE}:session:${Date.now()}:${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`,
704: 		method: "pane.report_agent_session",
705: 		params: {
706: 			pane_id: HERDR_PANE_ID,
707: 			source: HERDR_SOURCE,
708: 			agent: "pi",
709: 			seq: herdrNextSeq(),
710: 			session_start_source: sessionStartSource,
711: 			...sessionRef,
712: 		},
713: 	});
714: }
715:
716: function herdrSendState(state: HerdrAgentState, seq = herdrNextSeq()): Promise<void> {
717: 	return herdrSend({
718: 		id: `${HERDR_SOURCE}:${Date.now()}:${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`,
719: 		method: "pane.report_agent",
720: 		params: herdrWithSessionRef({
721: 			pane_id: HERDR_PANE_ID,
722: 			source: HERDR_SOURCE,
723: 			agent: "pi",
724: 			state,
725: 			seq,
726: 		}),
727: 	});
728: }
729:
730: function herdrQueueState(state: HerdrAgentState): void {
731: 	herdrQueued = { state, seq: herdrNextSeq() };
732: 	if (!herdrSendInFlight) void herdrDrainQueue();
733: }
734:
735: async function herdrDrainQueue(): Promise<void> {
736: 	if (herdrSendInFlight) return;
737: 	herdrSendInFlight = true;
738: 	try {
739: 		while (herdrQueued) {
740: 			const next = herdrQueued;
741: 			herdrQueued = undefined;
742: 			await herdrSendState(next.state, next.seq);
743: 		}
744: 	} finally {
745: 		herdrSendInFlight = false;
746: 		if (herdrQueued) void herdrDrainQueue();
747: 	}
748: }
749:
750: function herdrPublishState(state: HerdrAgentState, force = false): void {
751: 	if (!herdrEnabled()) return;
752: 	if (!force && state === herdrLastState) return;
753: 	herdrLastState = state;
754: 	herdrQueueState(state);
755: }

757: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
758: // Extension
759: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
760:
761: /** Threshold before showing elapsed time in status parentheses */
762: const SHOW_TIMER_AFTER_MS = 30_000;
763:
764: /** How long to preserve "thought for Ns" across turns */
765: const THOUGHT_DISPLAY_MS = 3_500;
766:
767: /** Minimum thinking duration before showing "thought for Ns" */
768: const MIN_THINKING_SHOW_MS = 100;
769:
770: /** Message refresh cadence. Keep constant so status updates don't stall on long sessions. */
771: const WORKING_MESSAGE_INTERVAL_MS = 1_000;
772:
773: /**
774:  * The "↓ N tokens" counter counts up to each new total instead of jumping there. Tokens arrive
775:  * in chunks (and a finished message swaps its estimate for the provider's real count), so the
776:  * shown number eases toward the real one: each frame closes the same share of the gap, about
777:  * 63% every TOKEN_EASE_MS, and at least one token, so a large jump takes about a second and a
778:  * steady stream is followed within a few tokens. Frames only run while the numbers differ.
779:  */
780: const TOKEN_FRAME_MS = 50;
781: const TOKEN_EASE_MS = 150;
782:
783: /** The counter's next value: `shown` moved toward `target` after `elapsedMs`, never past it. */
784: export function easeTokenCount(shown: number, target: number, elapsedMs: number): number {
785: 	const gap = target - shown;
786: 	if (gap === 0) return target;
787: 	const eased = Math.abs(gap) * (1 - Math.exp(-Math.max(0, elapsedMs) / TOKEN_EASE_MS));
788: 	const step = Math.max(1, Math.round(eased));
789: 	return step >= Math.abs(gap) ? target : shown + Math.sign(gap) * step;
790: }
791:
792: /** Completion message linger */
793: const TURN_COMPLETION_MS = 2_500;
794:

808: 	// thinking and tool-call arguments, so the count climbs as the model writes.

810: 	let streamedChars = 0;
811: 	let streamedBlockLengths: number[] = [];

813: 	let thinkingStartTime = 0;

821: 	// Root interactive session only — nested/non-UI contexts must not fight
822: 	// herdr state authority for this pane.
823: 	let herdrRootSession = false;
824:
825: 	function getEffortSuffix(): string {
826: 		try {
827: 			const level = pi.getThinkingLevel();

829: 			return ` with ${level} effort`;
830: 		} catch {
831: 			return "";
832: 		}
833: 	}
834:
835: 	function buildWorkingMessage(): string {
836: 		const elapsed = Date.now() - (agentStartTime || turnStartTime);
837: 		const tokenCount = shownTokens;
838: 		const statusParts: string[] = [];
839:
840: 		if (thinkingStatus === "thinking") {
841: 			statusParts.push(`thinking${getEffortSuffix()}`);
842: 		} else if (typeof thinkingStatus === "number") {
843: 			statusParts.push(`thought for ${Math.max(1, Math.round(thinkingStatus / 1000))}s`);
844: 		}
845:
846: 		if (tokenCount > 0) {
847: 			statusParts.push(`↓ ${formatCount(tokenCount)} tokens`);
848: 		}
849:
850: 		if (elapsed > SHOW_TIMER_AFTER_MS || thinkingStatus !== null || tokenCount > 0) {
851: 			statusParts.push(formatDuration(elapsed));
852: 		}
853:
854: 		const running = [...runningTools.values()];
855: 		const latest = running[running.length - 1];
856: 		const verb = latest
857: 			? `${describeToolActivity(latest.name, latest.args)}${running.length > 1 ? ` (+${running.length - 1} more)` : ""}`
858: 			: currentVerb;
859: 		let message = `${CLAUDE_ORANGE}${verb}…${RESET}`;
860: 		if (statusParts.length > 0) {
861: 			message += statusText(` (${statusParts.join(" · ")})`);
862: 		}
863: 		return message;
864: 	}
865:
866: 	function setStreamedBlockLength(index: number, length: number): void {
867: 		const previous = streamedBlockLengths[index] ?? 0;
868: 		streamedBlockLengths[index] = Math.max(0, length);
869: 		streamedChars = Math.max(0, streamedChars + streamedBlockLengths[index] - previous);
870: 	}
871:
872: 	function resetStreamed(): void {
873: 		streamedBlockLengths = [];
874: 		streamedChars = 0;
875: 	}
876:
877: 	function outputTokenCount(): number {
878: 		return runOutputTokens + Math.round(streamedChars / 4);
879: 	}
880:
881: 	/** Start of a top-level request (not steering or follow-ups inside it). */
882: 	function beginRun(now = Date.now()): void {
883: 		if (agentStartTime) return;

890: 	function resetShownTokens(): void {

895: 	function stopTokenAnimation(): void {
896: 		if (tokenFrameTimer) {
897: 			clearTimeout(tokenFrameTimer);

899: 		}

901:
902: 	/** Count the shown tokens toward the real total, one frame at a time, while they differ. */
903: 	function animateTokens(): void {
904: 		if (tokenFrameTimer || !turnActive || shownTokens === outputTokenCount()) return;
905: 		const scheduledAt = Date.now();

907: 			tokenFrameTimer = null;

909: 			syncWorkingMessage();

915: 	function syncWorkingMessage(force = false): void {
916: 		try {
917: 			if (!activeCtx?.hasUI) return;
918: 		} catch {
919: 			// Session replacement/reload invalidated the captured context.
920: 			return;
921: 		}
922: 		// Re-derive colors on every tick so /cc-spinner verb/status changes
923: 		// take effect within ~250 ms without waiting for the next pi event.
924: 		// applyThemeColors only re-resolves two theme colors, so this is cheap.
925: 		applyThemeColors(activeCtx.ui?.theme);

929: 		try {

931: 		} catch { /* noop */ }
932: 	}

934: 	function restoreDefaultWorkingMessage(): void {
935: 		lastWorkingMessage = null;
936: 		try {
937: 			if (!activeCtx?.hasUI) return;
938: 		} catch {
939: 			// Session replacement/reload invalidated the captured context.
940: 			return;
941: 		}
942: 		try {
943: 			activeCtx.ui.setWorkingMessage();
944: 		} catch { /* noop */ }

947: 	function getWorkingMessageIntervalMs(): number {
948: 		const elapsed = Date.now() - (agentStartTime || turnStartTime);
949: 		const tokenCount = outputTokenCount();
950: 		// Keep ticking once per second even when idle so /cc-spinner changes
951: 		// take effect within ~1s and elapsed-time crossover into the timer-on
952: 		// state still fires close to 30s. syncWorkingMessage short-circuits
953: 		// when the rendered string is unchanged, so the cost is negligible.
954: 		if (thinkingStatus === null && tokenCount === 0 && elapsed <= SHOW_TIMER_AFTER_MS) {
955: 			return Math.max(250, Math.min(WORKING_MESSAGE_INTERVAL_MS, SHOW_TIMER_AFTER_MS - elapsed + 1));
956: 		}
957: 		return Math.max(250, WORKING_MESSAGE_INTERVAL_MS - (elapsed % WORKING_MESSAGE_INTERVAL_MS));
958: 	}
959:
960: 	function scheduleRefreshTick(): void {
961: 		if (!turnActive || refreshTimer) return;

963: 		refreshTimer = setTimeout(() => {
964: 			refreshTimer = null;
965: 			syncWorkingMessage();

968: 		unrefTimer(refreshTimer);
969: 	}

## What the code already allows

Current behaviour, traced: `turn_start` calls `showWorkingStatusIndicator()` (interactive-mode.ts:3183) which builds `WorkingStatusIndicator(this.ui, "Working")` (2122-2135); the text never changes until `agent_end` clears it (3411). `Loader` (packages/tui/src/components/loader.ts) animates a braille glyph on an 80 ms interval and `setMessage()` repaints in place — `RetryStatusIndicator` already does exactly that from a `CountdownTimer` tick (status-indicator.ts:64-73). So the plugin's `Loader.prototype` monkey-patch (spinner.ts:158-205) is unnecessary here, and unwanted: we own this code path.

Where the line is drawn: `CustomEditor.renderTopBorder` (custom-editor.ts:60-104) with `borders: false` returns `" " + status`, i.e. the input band's top row. Phase 2 changes only the string, not the band.

## The three data sources Phase 2 needs, and what exists

1. **Running tool** — `tool_execution_start` gives `toolCallId`, `toolName`, `args`, `parentToolCallId` (nested calls skipped at 3366); `tool_execution_end` gives `result/isError/durationMs`. So `Running npm test…` is event-driven, not guessed. The plugin maps tools in `describeToolActivity` (spinner.ts:495-533).
2. **Token count** — `AssistantMessage.usage` has `input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, reasoning?, totalTokens, cost`. Mid-stream it is often still zeroed until a chunk carries usage, which is why the plugin counts streamed characters/4 as a live estimate and swaps in the provider's `usage.output` at `message_end` (spinner.ts:549-569, 1116-1171). That matches your plan's "counting up smoothly".
3. **Elapsed** — trivial, but note the plugin only shows the timer after 30 s (spinner.ts:762) while your plan wants `Transfiguring… 1.2k tokens · 4s` immediately.

## Differences from the plugin I would not copy

- It picks one verb per turn and keeps it for the whole run; your plan wants rotation every few seconds with no immediate repeat. Rotation is ours.
- It overrides the extension API `setWorkingMessage` by force. In toucan, extensions legitimately set that message (`interactive-mode.ts:2417-2422`), and a core engine rewriting the line every few seconds would stomp them.
- It carries ~500 lines of unrelated stuff (herdr socket reporting, theme file polling, prototype patches).

/** Spinner verbs shown while the model works, copied from pi-claude-code-ui (MIT). */

/**
 * Playful gerunds shown on the working line while nothing runs. Copied verbatim from
 * `pi-claude-code-ui` v1.0.109 (`FammasMaz/pi-cc-tools`, MIT), the source of the CC-UI port.
 */
export const SPINNER_VERBS = [ ... 230 ... ];

/** A verb to show now. The previous verb is never picked twice in a row. */
export function pickSpinnerVerb(previous?: string): string {
	if (SPINNER_VERBS.length === 1) return SPINNER_VERBS[0]!;
	let verb = previous;
	while (verb === previous) verb = SPINNER_VERBS[Math.floor(Math.random() * SPINNER_VERBS.length)]!;
	return verb;
}
```

Engine:

```ts
export interface WorkingStatusLine {
	/** Verb phrase without the trailing ellipsis, e.g. "Transfiguring" or "Running npm test". */
	verb: string;
	/** Status tail, e.g. "1.2k tokens · 4s". Empty when there is nothing to report. */
	status: string;
}

export interface WorkingStatusEngineOptions {
	onLine: (line: WorkingStatusLine) => void;
	now?: () => number;
	verbEveryMs?: number;
	tickEveryMs?: number;
	random?: () => number;   // for deterministic verb tests
}

const VERB_EVERY_MS = 5000;
const TICK_MS = 250;
const TOKENS_PER_CHAR = 1/4 → estimate = Math.round(chars/4)

export class WorkingStatusEngine {
	private readonly onLine; private readonly now; ...
	private verb = "";
	private running = new Map<string, {name: string; args: unknown}>();
	private blockLengths: number[] = [];
	private settledTokens = 0;
	private shownTokens = 0;
	private targetTokens = 0;
	private turnStartedAt = 0;
	private lastLineChangeAt = 0;   // for easing
	private tickTimer / rotateTimer
	private active = false;
	private frozen = false;   // an extension owns the line

	begin(): void   // turn_start
	end(): void     // agent_end / dispose: stop timers
	noteToolStart(id, name, args)
	noteToolEnd(id)
	setStreamedBlock(index, length)
	settleMessage(outputTokens: number)
	setFrozen(frozen: boolean)
	get line(): WorkingStatusLine   // computed
	dispose()
}
```

Verb selection: at `begin()`, pick verb. Rotation on tick when `now - verbAt >= verbEveryMs` and no tool running (if tools run, verb = tool phrase; when the tool ends, rotate immediately to a fresh verb).

Token easing: target = settledTokens + round(chars/4); shown eases toward target each tick (easeTokenCount-like). Emit on line when the emitted string changes.

Status tail: parts: `${formatTokens(shownTokens)} tokens` if >0; `${seconds}s` elapsed once >=1s. Join with " · ".

Emission policy: emit only when the composed line differs from the last emitted; call onLine.

Timers: `setInterval` for tick (TICK_MS), and rotation checked inside the same tick (no second timer) — simpler. Use unref? In a TUI process timers keep the event loop alive; Loader uses setInterval without unref, so consistent. But `dispose()` must clear.

Frozen: while frozen, no onLine calls (engine keeps state; when unfrozen, next tick emits).

Now tests (test/working-status.test.ts):
- verb rotates and never repeats consecutively (fake timers + injected random).
- tool running names the line: `Running npm test` after noteToolStart("1","bash",{command:"npm test"}); "+1 more" when two.
- token/elapsed tail: after setStreamedBlock(0, 400 chars) → 100 tokens; advance timers → shown eases to 100; tail contains "100 tokens · 1s".
- frozen suppresses.
- end() clears timers (no more onLine calls after end).

test/tool-activity.test.ts: mapping for bash/read/edit/write/grep/find/ls/mcp__srv__do_thing/unknown; clipping long commands (50).
