Keep the code clean, typed, no `any` (args: unknown with a helper reading string fields via Record<string, unknown> cast with a why comment... careful: AGENTS says no runtime checks of values TS guarantees, but args come from the wire/tool call as unknown → trust boundary, so validation is legitimate and must name the boundary).

`args: unknown` → helper:
```ts
function stringField(args: unknown, ...keys: string[]): string {
	// Tool arguments arrive from the model, not from a typed call site: read them defensively.
	const record = (args ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
	for (const key of keys) {
		const value = record[key];
		if (typeof value === "string" && value.trim()) return value.trim();
	}
	return "";
}
```

```ts
/** The working line: rotating verb or running-tool phrase, plus token and elapsed tail. */

import { formatTokens } from "./footer.ts";
import { describeToolActivity } from "./tool-activity.ts";
import { pickSpinnerVerb } from "../spinner-verbs.ts";

/** One render of the working line. Colors are the caller's job: verb accent, status muted. */
export interface WorkingStatusLine {
	verb: string;
	status: string;
}

export interface WorkingStatusOptions {
	onLine: (line: WorkingStatusLine) => void;
	now?: () => number;
	random?: () => number;
	/** How long one verb stays before a new one is picked. */
	verbEveryMs?: number;
	/** How often the line is recomputed for elapsed time and the counting token number. */
	tickEveryMs?: number;
}

const VERB_EVERY_MS = 5_000;
const TICK_MS = 250;
/**
 * The token number counts up instead of jumping: each tick closes a fixed share of the gap, so a
 * provider that reports usage in one chunk still produces a smooth climb. About 63% per EASE_MS.
 */
const EASE_MS = 150;

export class WorkingStatusEngine {
	...
}
```

Members & methods:
- `begin()`: active=true, turnStartedAt=now, verb=pick(undefined), verbAt=now, reset token state, start tick timer, emit.
- `end()`: active=false, stop timer, emit? no.
- `dispose()`: end.
- `noteToolStart(id, name, args)`: map.set, verbAt=now? The plan: while a tool runs, the line names it. Also when a tool ends, pick a fresh verb (so a stale verb doesn't return). Emit.
- `noteToolEnd(id)`: map.delete; if empty → new verb + verbAt=now. Emit.
- `setStreamedBlock(index, length)`: track block lengths, streamedChars; emit (throttled by change detection).
- `settleMessage(outputTokens)`: settledTokens += outputTokens; reset blocks; emit.
- `setFrozen(frozen)`: engine computes but does not call onLine; on unfreeze, emit current.
- `line(): WorkingStatusLine`.
- timers: `setInterval` tick; tick rotates verb when now-verbAt >= verbEveryMs && no tools, then emits.

Token easing math:
```ts
private easeTokens(now: number): void {
	const target = this.targetTokens();
	if (this.shownTokens === target) return;
	const gap = target - this.shownTokens;
	const eased = Math.abs(gap) * (1 - Math.exp(-Math.max(0, now - this.easeAt) / EASE_MS));
	const step = Math.max(1, Math.round(eased));
	this.shownTokens = step >= Math.abs(gap) ? target : this.shownTokens + Math.sign(gap) * step;
	this.easeAt = now;
}
```
target = settledTokens + Math.round(streamedChars/4).

status parts: tokens (`${formatTokens(shown)} tokens` when >0) and elapsed (`${Math.floor((now-start)/1000)}s` when >=1s) joined " · ".

Emission: keep `lastEmitted: {verb, status} | undefined`, compare.

Change detection for token easing: emit when either differs.

Timers must be cleared on end. Use setInterval; store id.

Extension override, as you chose: `setFrozen(true)` makes the engine keep state but stop emitting; unfreezing resumes on the next tick instead of leaving a blank line.

```ts
/** Characters the model has produced so far in a partial message: text, thinking, and tool-call arguments. */
export function streamedCharCount(message: AssistantMessage): number {
	let total = 0;
	for (const content of message.content) {
		if (content.type === "text") total += content.text.length;
		else if (content.type === "thinking") total += content.thinking.length;
		else if (content.type === "toolCall") total += JSON.stringify(content.arguments ?? {}).length;
	}
	return total;
}
```
Typed union → no defensive checks needed.

/**
 * Characters the model has produced in a streamed message: text, thinking, and tool-call
 * arguments. Used only to estimate output tokens while the provider has not reported them.
 */
export function estimateStreamedChars(message: AssistantMessage): number {
	let chars = 0;
	for (const content of message.content) {
		if (content.type === "text") chars += content.text.length;
		else if (content.type === "thinking") chars += content.thinking.length;
		else chars += JSON.stringify(content.arguments).length;
	}
	return chars;
}

	setWorkingStatusIndicator(indicator: StatusIndicator | undefined): void {
		this.workingStatusIndicator = indicator;
	}

	/**
	 * The solid input band has no border, so its status line floats above it: one status row,
	 * one blank row, and no editorBg on either, leaving only the input rows filled.
	 */
	protected override renderHeaderLines(width: number, hiddenLineCount: number): string[] {
		if (this.embedWorkingStatus && !this.borders && this.workingStatusIndicator && width > 0) {
			const status = this.workingStatusIndicator.renderInBorder(Math.max(1, width - 5));
			if (visibleWidth(status) > 0) return [truncateToWidth(` ${status}`, width, ""), ""];
		}
		return super.renderHeaderLines(width, hiddenLineCount);
	}

	protected override renderTopBorder(width: number, hiddenLineCount: number): string {
		if (!this.embedWorkingStatus || !this.workingStatusIndicator || width <= 0) {
			return super.renderTopBorder(width, hiddenLineCount);
		}

		let status = this.workingStatusIndicator.renderInBorder(Math.max(1, width - 5));
		let statusWidth = visibleWidth(status);
		if (statusWidth === 0) return super.renderTopBorder(width, hiddenLineCount);

		const overflowLabel = hiddenLineCount > 0 ? ` ↑ ${hiddenLineCount} more ` : undefined;
		const overflowLabelWidth = overflowLabel ? visibleWidth(overflowLabel) : 0;
		const overflowStart = Math.floor((width - overflowLabelWidth) / 2);
		const canFitOverflow = () =>
			overflowLabel !== undefined && overflowLabelWidth + 2 <= width && overflowStart - (3 + statusWidth + 1) >= 1;

## Background and position

The lighter fill came from `Editor.decorateLine`, which applied `lineBackground: editorBg` to every line the editor returns, including the status line the band renders above it. New hook in `packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts`:

```ts
protected renderHeaderLines(width, hiddenLineCount): string[]   // never background-painted
```
`render()` pushes those lines undecorated, so only the input rows keep the fill. `CustomEditor` overrides it for the borderless band and returns `[statusRow, ""]`, which is the extra blank row you asked for under the label. Row count is tracked in `renderedHeaderLines` and the click-to-cursor mapping now uses it, so clicking into the band still maps to the right visual line.

When no status is showing there is no header at all, so the band sits exactly where it did before.

One build note: coding-agent imports `@hyzek/toucan-tui` from its `dist/`, so the tui change needs `npm --prefix packages/tui run build` before coding-agent tests see it. That is what the first test run was missing, not a logic bug.
